title: The strict-local base-change mate is invertible on the closed stalk
statement: Let f:X→S be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let Ω be an algebraically closed field and s:Spec Ω→S a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let A be a henselian local ring with separably closed residue field κA [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let eA:Spec A≅strictHenselizationScheme(s) [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Put jA=eA.hom followed by strictHenselizationStructuralMap(s) [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Choose p0:X0→X and f0:X0→Spec A making a cartesian square over f,jA [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let k be any separably closed field and a:Spec k→Spec κA, and put t=a followed by the residue closed-point map Spec κA→Spec A. For any abelian étale sheaf G on X [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and q∈ℕ, let K=G[0]. The map on the geometric stalk at t [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] induced by H^q of the derived base-change mate D(jA)Rf_*K→Rf0_*D(p0)K [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange, def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is invertible. This assertion is about the one cartesian square over the strict-local structural map; there is no further cube or inverse image.

proof.text: Apply `isIso_strictHenselization_baseChange_globalHomology` to f, s, G[0], and q. The canonical derived mate there equals `derivedBaseChangeMapPlus`: compare their components on bounded-below complexes using `Adjunction.derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac` and `pullbackSquareComparison_hom_app_factorsh`, then use `derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_ext`. Thus global sections of homology of the canonical strict-local base-change map are invertible, without a torsion assumption.

Put j = strictHenselizationStructuralMap s, P = pullback f j, p = pullback.fst f j, and v = pullback.snd f j. The map b : X₀ → P is the pullback lift of p₀ and f₀ ≫ eA.hom. It satisfies b ≫ p = p₀ and b ≫ v = f₀ ≫ eA.hom. Pullback cancellation gives the cartesian square (b, f₀, v, eA.hom); because eA.hom is invertible, b is invertible too. Its derived base-change map is invertible: inverse image along an isomorphism is an exact equivalence preserving injectives, so `derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_fac_app` on an injective representative expresses this map as a composite of isomorphisms.

The horizontal pasting formula writes the outer mate at K = G[0] as C(eA.hom,j).hom followed by D(eA.hom) of the canonical mate, the mate of the square in step 2 at D(p)K, and R(f₀) of C(b,p).inv. Here C is `upperStarCompDerivedPlus`; the equation b ≫ p = p₀ identifies the outer square with sq₀. Global sections after inverse image along eA.hom are naturally isomorphic to global sections before it: whisker the invertible adjunction unit with global sections, and apply `lowerStarCompGlobalSectionsIso`. Homology commutes with exact inverse image by `mapDerivedCategoryPlusHomologyFunctorIso`. Consequently the middle factor remains invertible after global sections of homology, by step 1. All other factors are images of isomorphisms under functors. Thus global sections of homology of the sq₀ mate are invertible.

The point t = a followed by the residue closed-point map lies over the closed point of Spec A (`IsLocalRing.PrimeSpectrum.comap_residue`). Enlarge k to AlgebraicClosure k. `isIso_pointSmallEtalePrecomp_sheafFiber` and its naturality identify stalk maps before and after this enlargement. Apply `strictlyHenselianSections_geometricStalk_isIso` to the enlarged point and both homology sheaves. Its naturality states that the source global germ followed by the stalk map is the section map followed by the target global germ. The section map is invertible by step 3, using `ΓNatIsoSheafSections`. Both germs are invertible by 03QO. Cancel the source germ, then the field-extension comparison, to obtain invertibility of the displayed stalk map.
